answer.rationale:
Constraints prune the option set before memory does. rollback_release is the best-attested pattern (memory_b1, memory_b6) but is foreclosed by the compliance ruling on the security patch, so its strong track record is irrelevant here. add_capacity (memory_b3) worked as pre-provisioned headroom ahead of a known peak; we are already inside the peak, so it is a different operation than the one the memory actually vouches for. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) contained a failing external dependency; nothing here indicates partner failure, and failing fast on our own write path would shed exactly the settlement writes we are told not to lose.

That leaves regional_failover and route_read_replicas. memory_b2 is the surface-level match because the degradation is confined to the primary region, and that is precisely why I want it verified: the consolidated line says traffic 'shifted cleanly' and error rates recovered, but it says nothing about write volume, replication lag, or whether any in-flight writes were reconciled. A failover that was clean during the March latency event may not be clean at settlement peak with heavy writes, and the one thing I am told not to trade away is customer writes. There is also a causal problem: if the two-hour-old release is driving the regression, it is deployed in the failover target too, so I would move the load onto fresh infrastructure and reacquire the same defect while paying full cutover risk.

route_read_replicas (memory_b5) is the intervention whose mechanism matches the observed symptom most directly: offloading read/dashboard work reduced contention on the primary and write latency recovered same-day. I want b5 verified because the original record should say whether the relief came from contention reduction generically or specifically from heavy report queries that may not be present at settlement peak — if the primary's load is nearly all writes, the headroom recovered will be small and I need to know that before committing my single intervention.

I am running this as a small guarded test: ramp a bounded slice of read traffic off the primary, watch write p99 and replica lag, and keep it trivially reversible. It cannot lose writes, it does not fight the compliance constraint, and it preserves the failover option for the next window with better information. If verification shows b5's relief was report-query-specific and inapplicable, and b2 shows the March cutover was validated under write-heavy load with no write loss, I would switch to regional_failover.

Downstream value risk: whatever I do here gets consolidated into this same durable memory in one compressed line. The current entries have already lost the conditions that made each action safe — b2 does not record write volume, b3 does not record that it was pre-peak. If I act on the region-shaped surface match and it happens to work, the archive gains 'failover fixed the day-74 write degradation' and the write-loss exposure I never actually tested becomes invisible to the next agent. I would rather log the mechanism, the load profile, and the untested assumption than a clean verdict.
